topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate of Change: Understanding the Derivative

outline.topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate of Change: Understanding the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem: Average vs. Instantaneous
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'average speed' (total distance/total time). Explain that while we can measure average speed over an interval, life happens in an instant. Set the stage for why we need a new mathematical tool to capture speed at a single, frozen moment.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: We know its average speed over 10 seconds, but how fast is it moving at exactly the 3-second mark?

sections.title: Visualizing the Slope: The Secant Line
sections.content: Introduce a position-time graph. Show a secant line connecting two points on a curve. Explain that the slope of this line represents the average rate of change. Use an animation of one point sliding closer to the other to visually demonstrate the interval shrinking.
sections.example: A position-time curve of a rocket launch. Drawing a straight line through two points on the curve shows average velocity between those two times.

sections.title: The Limit: Shrinking the Interval
sections.content: Define the 'Limit' concept: As the time interval approaches zero, the secant line morphs into a tangent line. Emphasize that the slope of this tangent line is the instantaneous rate of change.
sections.example: An animation showing the secant line rotating and flattening as the two points merge into one point, finally becoming a single tangent line at the 3-second mark.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the concept. Present the derivative formula: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect the symbols back to the 'rise over run' concept, explaining that h is the tiny 'time gap' being squashed to zero.
sections.example: Display the mathematical formula overlaying the graphical tangent line to show that the 'limit' is simply the precise calculation of that slope.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the graphical (slope of tangent) and algebraic (the limit) perspectives. Explain that the derivative is the universal tool for measuring how things change at any precise instant.
sections.example: Showing a speedometer in a self-driving car: The computer calculates the derivative of the position function thousands of times per second to provide the exact instantaneous speed.

lecture_lines: Average speed uses total distance and time.
But life changes in an instant.
We need speed at a single moment.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Slope: The Secant Line
lecture_lines: A secant line connects two points.
Its slope shows average rate of change.
Slide one point closer to shrink the gap.
animations: Draw a curve and two points [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] (A, B) connected by a secant line (#FFFF00).
Highlight the slope triangle between points A and B. Label 'Slope' in #00FFFF color.
Move point B [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] along the curve closer to A, shrinking the gap.

storyboard.title: The Limit: Shrinking the Interval
lecture_lines: The secant line becomes a tangent.
This slope is the instantaneous rate.
animations: Show the gap between points approaching zero. Label 'h -> 0' in #FFFFFF color. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Animate the secant line morphing into a tangent line (#FF00FF).
Flash the tangent line to emphasize 'Instantaneous slope' at that point.

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: Derivative formula: f'(x) is a limit.
It measures change as h becomes zero.
It calculates the exact slope perfectly.
animations: Display limit formula: lim(h->0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Color code variables in #00FF00.
Show 'h' shrinking to zero using a slider visual [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slider.svg]. Label 'h -> 0' in #FF0000.
Display result f'(x) near the curve, highlighting the slope calculation in #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: The derivative combines slope and limits.
It measures change at any precise instant.
animations: Show a collage of slope and limit icons merging into one derivative symbol.
Flash the derivative symbol over a graph representing movement. Label 'f'(x)' in #00FFFF.
